subject: Token delivery jitter impacting interactive sessions (FastLane) - temporary mitigations applied
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir@fastlane.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [FastLane] Intermittent token "jitter" in chat during peak - examples attached

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Over the last 90 minutes we've seen our live conversation sessions for the checkout-flow assistant show bursts where tokens take 800ms-1.2s each to arrive (we call it "jitter"). The UI shows long pauses and then a bunch of tokens in quick succession. This started around 06:30 UTC and coincided with our traffic spike.

Attached is an abbreviated trace for one session (fastlane-trace-20270707.json). We're on SDK v3.1.2 using streaming chunked responses with default config. No code changes on our side. Can you confirm whether this looks like client-side batching or a server-side token pacing issue, and any short-term mitigation we can apply? This is impacting a handful of paying customers during peaks.

Thanks,
Samir Kapoor
Head of Platform
FastLane AI

Attachments: fastlane-trace-20270707.json (trace export)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [FastLane] Intermittent token "jitter" in chat during peak - examples attached

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick trace. We're prioritizing this. Initial read: traces show steady server-side token generation time spikes coincident with a small subset of short-running models in your routing policy.

Short-term mitigations you can try while we triage:
- Set per-connection concurrency to 1 in your client (reduces interleaving pressure).
- Add header x-redwood-prefer-variant: low_latency_v2 to prefer our low-latency model variant.
- Reduce streaming chunk size to 64 tokens (SDK param: chunk_size=64).

I'll coordinate with ops to apply a temporary routing preference and bump priority for your session pool. Can you confirm the SDK version and whether you can attempt the header change now?

I'll update in ~25 minutes with what ops does.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FastLane token jitter - propose temporary routing + autoscaler tweak

Monica / Ben — Samir at FastLane reporting token-level jitter for interactive sessions (trace attached). Customer traffic spike correlates with a small fraction of requests routed to the 'general-purpose' variant that shows higher tail token latency under burst.

Proposed immediate actions (short-lived, safe rollback):
1) Apply a temporary routing override for account DL-8342 to prefer low_latency_v2 (model alias: rwd-lowlat-v2-fp16) for the next 60 minutes.
2) Reduce per-connection concurrency to 1 for that session pool (routing metadata override).
3) Patch autoscaler to give temporary token-throughput headroom: increase burst pool size by +2 GPU units for 1 hour.

I'm attaching the ops note I'll send to the customer once you've confirmed changes. Risk: small possibility of slightly higher cost for the hour.

Attachments: temp-routing-change.txt

Please reply when done.
— Avery

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 08:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: FastLane token jitter - propose temporary routing + autoscaler tweak

Avery — on it. Actions executed at 08:46 PDT:
- Added routing override for DL-8342: prefer rwd-lowlat-v2-fp16.
- Inserted per-connection concurrency metadata (1) for that account's session pool.
- Increased burst pool capacity by +2 GPU units for 60 minutes (autoscaler policy inf-burst-34 updated).

Logs: autoscaler adjustment applied (autoscaler-adjustment.diff). No rollout to other accounts. Monitoring is Green/Amber depending on the pool. Will watch token throughput metrics and report back in 10m.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [FastLane] Intermittent token "jitter" in chat during peak - examples attached

Samir — quick update and what we changed (effective 08:46 PDT):
- Temporarily routed DL-8342 sessions to our low-latency variant (alias: rwd-lowlat-v2-fp16).
- Applied per-connection concurrency=1 for your session pool to reduce interleaving pressure.
- Bumped burst capacity by +2 GPU units for 60 minutes to absorb peak token bursts.

What we'd like you to try right now:
1) If possible, set header x-redwood-prefer-variant: low_latency_v2 in your requests. Example: curl -H "x-redwood-prefer-variant: low_latency_v2" ...
2) Reduce chunk size to 64 tokens (SDK param chunk_size=64).

Expected impact: token arrival times should normalize within a few connection exchanges (we saw median token time drop from ~400ms to ~90ms in similar repro). If you still see jitter after applying the header, reply here with one short trace and we will escalate to deeper profiling.

We've opened internal ticket INF-2739 and will follow up with a short postmortem. Apologies for the disruption — we'll include permanent remediation plans in the postmortem (model selection logic and autoscaler tweaks).

Thanks for the quick reports and the trace.
— Avery
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Kapoor <samir@fastlane.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [FastLane] Intermittent token "jitter" in chat during peak - examples attached

Avery / team — thanks, I can confirm the sessions I tested after 08:50 show much smoother token arrival (no visible pauses). The curl header change did the trick for our immediate tests.

Can you please share the INF ticket number and an ETA for the postmortem? We'd like a short write-up we can share with our ops team. Also please confirm whether the temporary routing will be rolled back automatically after 60 minutes.

— Samir
